title: From Jumps to Signatures: A Generative Method for Temporal Point Processes
claim: Jump-based event paths can be lifted into continuous bounded-variation paths by an injective embedding that encodes interarrival durations.
layout: 1 panel, time on x-axis, step path overlaid with embedding curve
description: A single line plot titled 'Counting path η_t and embedding Φ'. The x-axis is time t from 0 to 7. The y-axis runs from 0 to 7. A solid dark-blue staircase shows the counting path of a Poisson process: it jumps by one at each event, with the jumps clustered near t≈6. A dashed green piecewise-linear curve shows the embedding Φ(η)_t. It rises from 0 to 3 at t≈3.5, which is the length of the long interarrival gap. It then falls and wiggles near zero as the events bunch up, and it ends near 0.9 at t=7. Orange-red dots mark grid points (t_k, τ_k) where the embedding has its vertices. A legend in the upper left names the three elements. The eye goes first to the contrast between the blue steps and the green zigzag.
caption: Illustration of the interarrival embedding $\Phi$ (Definition [ref]) for a sampled Poisson process ($\lambda=1$, $\Tmax = 7$). Orange dots show the duration of the most recent interarrival interval.
abstract: Rough path signatures are a universal feature map for continuous paths and, via the expected signature, characterise path distributions. These guarantees do not directly extend to cadlag paths of Temporal Point Processes (TPPs), limiting the use of signature methods for event sequences. Furthermore, neural TPP models, including recent generative approaches, optimise per-event objectives with no global sequence-level loss, while evaluation of variable-length event sequences lacks distributional discrepancy measures. This paper proposes a common pathwise framework for addressing these limitations. We introduce the interarrival embedding, a stable, injective lift from jump paths to continuous paths of bounded variation, extending signature methods to discrete event sequences. Our theoretical contributions give rise to sigTPP, the first signature-based generative model for TPPs, trained using a path-level loss on complete trajectories. We further analyse the space of counting paths and derive $3$ distributional discrepancies, providing mathematically justified tools for evaluating generative TPP models. Across $12$ tasks, sigTPP achieves the best mean rank based on $8$ complementary metrics, outperforms or is within one standard error of the strongest baseline (which varies based on performance) in $57\%$ of the dataset-metric pairs, and according to a relative score, improves against each baseline by at least $24\%$ on average.
